business_interpretation: Are local governments preempted from regulating UAS operation (takeoff, landing, drone ports)?
known_limitation: Airspace itself is federal (DR_FED_PREEMPTION_AIRSPACE); state preemption concerns local land-use and ordinance exposure; Florida also protects drone-delivery drone ports

business_interpretation: Can a vehicle legally operate with no human driver on board in the state?
known_limitation: Absence of a statute (NO_SPECIFIC_STATUTE) is not prohibition and is not favorable; Kansas adds a 12-month in-vehicle driver phase-in per entity (see RT_SAFETY_DRIVER_REQUIREMENT); New York and Illinois codes rest on blocked or secondary sources (LOW)

business_interpretation: Is there a legal path to carry paying passengers in driverless vehicles?
known_limitation: Highly correlated with RT-01 across states; Phase 7 must decide whether to combine (e.g. ordinal) or keep one. Michigan limits on-demand networks to manufacturer SAVE fleets; Pennsylvania adds PUC authority

business_interpretation: Are cities preempted from restricting AV operation or AV for-hire service?
known_limitation: Preemption is favorable only where operation is authorized; local police powers survive in most preemption clauses; NOT_ADDRESSED leaves local exposure uncertain

business_interpretation: Does state law authorize personal delivery devices?
known_limitation: NO_STATUTE is absence, not prohibition: local permits may still allow operation (e.g. California cities); Nevada's statute is limited to university campuses (scope note in evidence)

business_interpretation: Can local governments prohibit or condition PDD operation?
known_limitation: Only meaningful where SW-01 authorizes PDDs; several codes rest on inference from compliance-with-local-rules clauses (MEDIUM)
Weight bases differ (with or without cargo; see analyst_note); D.C.'s 250 lb cap is temporary (expires 2027-04-02); not applicable where no PDD statute exists
